primary.title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
primary.author: Adam Smith
primary.rationale: Smith's most famous and influential work, laying the foundation for classical economics. It is widely available in digital formats.

primary.title: The Theory of Moral Sentiments
primary.author: Adam Smith
primary.rationale: Smith's earlier major work, exploring ethics and human sympathy. It is also a foundational text and available digitally.

primary.title: Essays on Philosophical Subjects
primary.author: Adam Smith
primary.rationale: A posthumously published collection of essays covering various philosophical topics, offering insights into Smith's broader intellectual interests.

secondary.title: Adam Smith's Political Economy: Foundations for a Free Society
secondary.author: Michael D. Bordo
secondary.rationale: A recent scholarly book examining Smith's economic thought and its relevance to contemporary issues, published by a major academic press.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Adam Smith
secondary.author: Roderick Long and Jennifer Welchman
secondary.rationale: An edited collection of essays by leading scholars providing a comprehensive overview of Smith's life, work, and influence.

secondary.title: Adam Smith and the Wealth of Nations: A Reader's Guide
secondary.author: James R. Otteson
secondary.rationale: A scholarly guide designed to help readers understand Smith's magnum opus, offering critical analysis and historical context.

suggestions.notes: Adam Smith's major works are foundational to economics and moral philosophy and are readily available in digital archives. The secondary sources focus on recent academic interpretations and comprehensive companions to his work.
